papers.title: On Uncertainty Quantification of Lithium-ion Batteries: Application to an LiC$_6$/LiCoO$_2$ cell
papers.abstract: In this work, a stochastic, physics-based model for Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is presented in order to study the effects of parametric model uncertainties on the cell capacity, voltage, and concentrations. To this end, the proposed uncertainty quantification (UQ) approach, based on sparse polynomial chaos expansions, relies on a small number of battery simulations. Within this UQ framework, the identification of most important uncertainty sources is achieved by performing a global sensitivity analysis via computing the so-called Sobol' indices. Such information aids in designing more efficient and targeted quality control procedures, which consequently may result in reducing the LIB production cost. An LiC$_6$/LiCoO$_2$ cell with 19 uncertain parameters discharged at 0.25C, 1C and 4C rates is considered to study the performance and accuracy of the proposed UQ approach. The results suggest that, for the considered cell, the battery discharge rate is a key factor affecting not only the performance variability of the cell, but also the determination of most important random inputs.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要研究锂电池的不确定性量化，与用户的生物力学植入物方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA or structural mechanics context; the battery model is not transferable to implant/biomechanics surrogate modelling due to fundamentally different physics and lack of geometric/contact nonlinearities.

summary_zh.motivation: 量化锂电池参数不确定性对性能的影响

summary_zh.validation: 通过不同放电率下的仿真案例验证方法准确性

summary_en.motivation: To quantify the effects of parametric uncertainties on lithium-ion battery capacity, voltage, and concentrations using a stochastic physics-based model.
summary_en.method: A sparse polynomial chaos expansion approach is employed for uncertainty quantification and global sensitivity analysis via Sobol' indices.
summary_en.result: The battery discharge rate is identified as a key factor affecting performance variability and the ranking of most important random inputs.
summary_en.validation: The approach is validated through simulation cases at 0.25C, 1C, and 4C discharge rates.
